original.target_description: Finnish nationwide nested case–control study; primary full text could not be obtained.

replication.target_description: Swedish nationwide matched conditional logistic regression of breast cancer and antipsychotic exposure; identical supplied locators do not distinguish among multiple exposure/model/subgroup tests.

reported_success.location: Discussion, first paragraph (comparison with the Finnish nationwide study)
reported_success.quote: These findings are consistent with those of a similar nested case–control study previously conducted in Finland

notes: All four assigned records supply identical neutral descriptions and p. 5 locators, without exposure duration/category, adjusted versus unadjusted model, cancer subtype, or population subgroup identifiers. The replication full text is available and its identity verified against Europe PMC DOI/title metadata (PMC11548924). Multiple distinct matching candidate tests are printed; assigning them among IDs by order would be unsupported. Replication Table 2, adjusted OR column, prints prolactin-increasing 1–<5 years: 1.20 (1.03–1.41), ≥5 years: 1.47 (1.26–1.71); prolactin-sparing 1–<5 years: 1.17 (0.98–1.40), ≥5 years: 0.99 (0.78–1.26). These are candidate observations only, not selected effects. Table 2 also prints unadjusted models; Table 3 prints cumulative-dose models and Table 5 subgroup models. No exact p values are supplied for the Table 2 candidate ORs; no p values derived from confidence intervals. Results/Table 1 identify 1642 breast-cancer cases and 8173 matched controls; a specific target model/sample cannot be selected. Original full primary source unavailable after DOI landing redirect, Unpaywall (closed; no OA locations), OpenAlex (closed; no repository full text), Europe PMC (no full text), Helsinki repository metadata only, and ScienceDirect 403. Original values quoted in the replication were not substituted for original primary evidence. Narrative success is study-level, independently stated in the replication Discussion; it does not resolve which effect each audit ID targets.
